I am writing to express my serious concern regarding the difficulties I have faced today in securing an appointment for an urgent, ongoing medical condition I have been managing for six months.
Chronology of Events:
• 09:15 AM: I spoke with a receptionist at Handsworth Wood Medical Centre. She informed me she would send a "rapid link" via text/email so I could book an appointment online.
• Follow-up: After waiting significant amount of time and not receiving the link, I attempted to call back. I was placed at number nine in the queue and was not offered a call-back option.
• Online Attempt: I tried using a previous booking link I had on file. However, after completing the triage questions, the system only offered appointments at "ENKI," which is the incorrect medical centre.

My Concerns:
1. Administrative Failure: The promised link was never sent. Whether this was an oversight or a technical error, it is unacceptable given the urgency of my health issue.
2. System Accuracy: The online portal is directing patients to the wrong facility, making it impossible to complete a booking for this practice.
3. Professional Standards: This experience suggests a need for administrative review or further staff training to ensure patients are not left without access to care.
I would appreciate it if you could look into why the link was not sent and, more importantly, arrange an urgent appointment for me today.
I look forward to your immediate response.
Sincerely,
Mr. Gogna
Is this normal practice?

"Maladministration" is a strong word, but my experience today, is right to point out that a breakdown in communication for an urgent case is a serious matter.

Could you please investigate this matter and also arrange for me to see a GP with reference to my medical issues issues. The issue in question is related to my last appointment and visit to the surgery to see a GP regarding discolouration infection of the skin on my penis. I look forward to your urgent reply back to me.
